topic: Claude Code Auto Mode Safety Guide 2026: Destructive Commands, Sandbox, and Production Hardening

competitors.title: How we built Claude Code auto mode: a safer way to skip permissions
key_points: Auto mode uses two-layer defense: input-layer prompt-injection probe and output-layer transcript classifier on Sonnet 4.6
Two-stage classification: fast single-token filter (8.5% FPR, 6.6% FNR on real traffic) then chain-of-thought reasoning (0.4% FPR, 17% FNR)
Classifier sees only user messages and tool calls — strips assistant text and tool results for injection robustness
Threat model covers: overeager behavior, honest mistakes, prompt injection, and misaligned models
Deny-and-continue: blocked actions trigger retry, not session kill; 3 consecutive or 20 total denials escalate to human
Multi-agent handoffs: classifier runs at both delegation and return of subagent tasks
93% of permission prompts are accepted in practice — auto mode targets the remaining 7% of dangerous actions

competitors.title: Claude Code Permissions — Official Documentation
key_points: Tiered permission system: read-only (no approval), Bash commands (yes), file modification (yes, until session end)
Permission modes: default, acceptEdits, plan, auto, dontAsk, bypassPermissions
Permission rules follow format Tool or Tool(specifier) with wildcard support
Deny rules evaluated first, then ask, then allow — first match determines outcome
Bare tool name deny (e.g. Bash) removes tool from context entirely; scoped deny (Bash(rm *)) blocks matching calls
Protected paths never auto-approved in any mode except bypassPermissions
Read-only commands (ls, cat, grep, etc.) run without prompt in every mode

competitors.title: Claude Code Sandboxed Bash Tool — Official Documentation
key_points: Bash sandbox uses OS-level enforcement: Seatbelt on macOS, bubblewrap on Linux/WSL2
Two sandbox modes: auto-allow (commands run without permission) and regular permissions (all commands go through flow)
Default write: current working directory + session temp directory only
Default read: entire computer except certain denied directories (includes ~/.aws and ~/.ssh by default)
Network isolation via proxy server — no domains pre-allowed, prompts on first access
Escape hatch: dangerouslyDisableSandbox parameter for commands that fail under sandbox
Strict mode: allowUnsandboxedCommands=false disables escape hatch entirely
Requires bubblewrap and socat packages on Linux

competitors.title: Claude Code Permission Modes — Official Documentation
key_points: Auto mode available on Pro plan (v2.1.143+) and Team/Enterprise with admin enable
Auto mode requires Claude Opus 4.6+ or Sonnet 4.6 on Anthropic API; Opus 4.7/4.8 on Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry
Classifier blocks by default: curl|bash, sensitive data exfiltration, production deploys, mass cloud deletion, IAM changes, force push, git reset --hard, terraform/pulumi/cdk destroy
Classifier allows by default: local file ops, declared dependency installs, credential reads to matching APIs, read-only HTTP, pushing to session branch
User-stated boundaries in conversation treated as block signals by classifier
Auto mode pauses after 3 consecutive or 20 total denials, resumes on manual approval

competitors.title: Configure Auto Mode — Official Documentation
key_points: autoMode.environment defines trusted infrastructure: repos, buckets, domains the classifier treats as internal
Three customizable rule slots: hard_deny (unconditional), soft_deny (overridable by user intent), allow (exceptions)
$defaults literal splices built-in rules at that position for incremental customization
Classifier reads autoMode from user settings, local settings, and managed settings — NOT from shared project settings
claude auto-mode defaults/config/critique subcommands for inspection and validation
Environment section should cover: organization, source control, cloud providers, trusted buckets, internal domains, key services

stats.fact: Auto mode uses a separate Sonnet 4.6 classifier model that evaluates each action before execution, running independently of the main Claude model
Bash sandbox on Linux requires bubblewrap and socat packages; on macOS uses built-in Seatbelt framework
Sandbox default write access: current working directory and session temp directory only; default read: entire computer except denied paths
Sandbox network isolation uses a proxy server with no pre-allowed domains — first access to each domain triggers a permission prompt
Auto mode available on Pro plan since v2.1.143 (May 2026) and on Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry since v2.1.158 (June 2026)
Auto mode requires Claude Opus 4.6+ or Sonnet 4.6 on Anthropic API; Opus 4.7/4.8 on third-party providers
Protected paths (repository state, Claude's own config) are never auto-approved in any mode except bypassPermissions
Permission rules follow deny→ask→allow precedence; a broad deny like Bash(aws *) blocks all matching calls including those matching a narrower allow rule
Sandbox auto-allow mode and auto mode are independent — auto-allow approves Bash because sandbox contains it, auto mode uses a classifier
Managed settings can enforce sandbox with failIfUnavailable=true and allowUnsandboxedCommands=false for organization-wide compliance
Auto mode classifier blocks: downloading/executing code (curl|bash), sending sensitive data externally, production deploys, mass cloud deletion, IAM changes, force push, git reset --hard
Auto mode classifier allows: local file operations, declared dependency installs, credential reads to matching APIs, read-only HTTP, pushing to session branch
After 3 consecutive or 20 total classifier denials, auto mode pauses and resumes manual prompting
Sandbox escape hatch (dangerouslyDisableSandbox) can be disabled via allowUnsandboxedCommands: false in managed settings
Auto mode configuration supports hard_deny (unconditional), soft_deny (overridable by user intent), and allow (exceptions) rule slots
